title: 1969 AHSME Problem 14
statement: The complete set of \(x\)-values satisfying the inequality \(\dfrac{x^2-4}{x^2-1}\gt0\) is the set of all \(x\) such that:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(x\) is any real number except \(1\) or \(-1\)

solutions.text:
Factor the expression as \[ \frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{(x-1)(x+1)}. \] A sign chart at \(-2,\) \(-1,\) \(1,\) and \(2\) shows it is positive on \[ (-\infty,-2)\cup(-1,1)\cup(2,\infty). \] The endpoints \(\pm2\) give zero and \(\pm1\) are undefined.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: The sign can change only at \(-2,\) \(-1,\) \(1,\) and \(2\)
Test one point in each interval and exclude zeros and undefined points
